label: paragraph_title
text: REFERENDUM GOES AGAINST HIM

label: text
text: AUSTRALIA'S VOICE

label: text
text:
The referendum in Australia on two Constitutional amendments submitted by the Federal Government empowering the "Government" to make laws applying to corporations of all kinds regulating labour conditions throughout the "Commonwealth," establishing the authority of the Federal Courts to conciliate and arbitrate in all trade disputes, and enabling the Government to protect the interests of the public in the event of a actual or probable interruption of any essential service, has resulted in a large majority against both proposals.
Mr. S. M. Ervoe, the Prime Minister on being asked what he would do as the result of the referendum defeat, replied that since the people had said "No" there was nothing further to be done. Reute

label: paragraph_title
text: Melbourne Sept. 6.

label: text
text: Poubts have been expressed in certain quarters regarding the intentions of the Government of India in the matter of maintaining exchange at £5,500 per rupee in view of the post-payment of the consideration of Currency Bills in the legislature.

label: text
text: The Government of India has now issued its communicative stating that in accordance with the announcement made on August 4, it will continue to take such steps as may be necessary to prevent any value of the repro in order to co-value the movement of exchange within approximate upper and lower gold points as calculated on the basis of a gold repro at 16,15d, that is to say between the Fs. 6.9-15d. and Fs. label: paragraph_title
text: LENGIEN'S CHOICE.

label: text
text:
WIMBLEDON ONLY FOR THE
RICH.

label: text
text:
The Pourville Correspondent of the "Daily Mail" writes:
"Will my social status be affected?" Why, no, I should think not judging by the number of telegrams I have received today. We have been swamped by them since seven o'clock this morning.

label: text
text: With these words, Melle, Langlen received me here to day, and explained why she had turned to professional.

label: text
text: We were sitting in an oak panelled dining-room where she signed the contract to give a exhibition matches for money. The agreement stipulates that she is to make a four-months tour in the United States, Canada, Cuba and Mexico.

label: text
text: For years," she said, "Americans have been pestering me to turn professional, and at last, when I was at Nice last year, I agreed to consider a proposal from an agent of Mr. C. C. Pyle, with whom the contract was signed.

label: paragraph_title
text: Ridiculous Rules.

label: text
text: “I refused to give an immediate reply. When Mr. D'yle himself crossed the Atlantic, however, I agreed to his terms. And why should I not? I think I have been an amateur long enough.

label: text
text: "Amateur tennis rules are ridiculous. They make provision only for the rich. If you are poor you cannot play in the amateur championships. An association ought to be formed of amateurs who refuse" to abide by the absurdly severe amateur rules.

label: text
text: "They ought to say, 'We will play against whom we like, whether our opponents are amateurs or professionals. We want to be matched against the best class of players, not the best class of social rank.'". I asked her if she would ever play against amateurs again.

label: text
text:
"I do not see how I can," she replied, "until the rules are altered."
"Oh course, I shall not be able to play again at Wimbledon, but I am not sorry. The organisers of these big amateur tennis championships take all the profits and yet treat the players just like professionals. Sometimes they are hardly civil."

label: text
text: Mile. Lenglen said that tennis should be treated on the same lines as golf, that open tennis matches should be held in which professionals and amateurs should play together. Why was there, a distinction between the two games, she asked.

label: text
text: Milla. Lenglen, whose right arm has troubled her since she caught cold when playing in the French championships, and which caused her to scratch at Wimbledon this year, intends to resume practice to-morrow.

label: text
text:
CONSERVATION MEASURE IN
USA

label: text
text: ONLY SIX YEARS SUPPLY.

label: text
text: Washington, September 6.

label: text
text: In a preliminary report to President Coalitionize the Federal Oil Conservation Board recommends legislation "legislating " the unit pool operation" for oil properties as a means of re-organising the production of oil.

label: text
text: The report adds that there is only six years' supply in the provided funds, and calls attention to the need for immediate conservation of measures.—Keuter.

label: text
text: In its report the Board calls attention to the promising oilfields in Mexico and South America. It states that the matter is of the first importance to United States companies, who should vigorously acquire and explore such fields not only as a source of future supply but of a supply controlled by United States citizens.

label: paragraph_title
text: Outside Supplies.

label: text
text: It declares that the country should not become dependent on foreign countries for oil supplies.

label: text
text: SIGNIFICANT SPEECH.

label: text
text: The Assembly by 42 out of 48 votes elected M. Nintchitch, the Yugo Slavian Foreign Minister, an President.

label: text
text: Geneva, Sept. 6.

label: text
text: M. Nintchitch, in a speech expressed Yugo-Slavia's attachment to the League's the guardian of peace and civilisation, "It's hoped that the clouds which had darkened the horizon for the last few months would be dissipated." "The imminent presence of an additional great nation among us should afford us full confidence."

label: text
text: The above allusion to Germany's entry to the League is all the more significant coming from the lips of a representative of a country which suffered at the hands of Germany in the Great War.

label: text
text: The League Assembly Credentials Committee is composed of eight delegates, and includes M. Wangkingky. --Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Policy of Conelliation.

label: text
text:
The opening speech of the Czecho-Slovakian Premier, M. Benes, at the Assembly of the League has been wirelessly broadcast.
A Geneva report states that M. Benes said that the League ever since its creation had been concerned with the problem of disarmament which was appreciably nearer the goal. The members of the league, in response to the Assembly's recommendation, were inaugurating among themselves a vast new political system based on the principle of conciliation and arbitration.

label: text
text: As regards organisation the Council report, which had been adopted, seemed to hold out a prospect of a, unanimous speedy agreement. A cordial welcome would be extended to-morrow to the League's new member—Germany. They were saddened by the thought of the departure of Staples which were very dear to them, but they had not yet lost all hope.—Renter.

label: paragraph_title
text: MEXICO TO EFFECT ECONOMIES.

label: text
text: TREATIES TO LARSE.

label: text
text:
Mexico City, Sept. 6.
President Calles is co-operating with the Chambers of Commerce in an effort to relieve the economic situation. He has instructed the Government Departments not to purchase abroad products which can be procured in Mexico.

label: text
text: The Foreign Office has reiterated its intention not to renew the Treaties of amity and commerce with Great Britain, France, Germany, and other countries, expiring this year, but expressed its willingness to negotiate for new Treaties.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: FASCISM OPPOSED

label: paragraph_title
text: TO BE DRIVEN FROM FACE OF EARTH.

label: text
text: ENEMY OF HUMANITY

label: text
text: “The Federation will stand and work with the Anti-Fascist Alliance of North America until Fascism is driven from the face of the earth” declared Mr. William Green, President of the American Federation of Labour, in addressing 500 delegates at the first annual convention of the Alliance.

label: text
text: Mr. Green said that he had come purposely to show the deep sympathy of the workers with anti-Fascism, declaring that Fascism was an enemy of society and humanity.--Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: STRIKE" PICKETS.

label: paragraph_title
text:
WHAT THEY HAVE DONE
SINCE SATURDAY.

label: text
text: ACTIVE ON SHORE?

label: text
text:
Since Saturday when the British senior naval officer of the West River dislodged the Canton strike pickets from the Steamboat Co.'s wharf, there have been several movements.
Several of the pickets were arrested for trespassing, it is stated.
The examination shed' established by the "Labour and Merchants' Examination Bureau," on the Tung On Co.'s wharf, has closed down; but a similar establishment may have been erected elsewhere.

label: text
text: Pickets have now taken up positions, near the bund, but at a safe distance from the Naval detachments and patrols.

label: text
text: Canton police and gendarmes are preserving order in the neighbourhood.

label: text
text: The Canton Foreign Ministry has communicated with the Strike Executive which has, in turn, instructed members not to enter foreign buildings.

label: text
text: The Executive has asked the Ministry to lodge a protest.

label: text
text:
Ministry to lodge a protest.
The pro-Kuomintang (four) Chambers of Commerce of Canton have passed four resolutions, asking for a protest and the withdrawal of the warships and British armed launches.

label: text
text: Telegrams from, Canton state that there is complete cessation of firing by pickets' boats which disappeared at the first sign of activity by British naval vessels. The latter found it unnecessary to fire a single shot.

label: text
text: Although ejected from the British wharf alongside which gunboats have been stationed, pickets are still showing activity ashore. British Wireless Service

label: paragraph_title
text: QUEER CHOW.

label: text
text: ARMADILXO SOLD HERE FOR FOOD.

label: text
text: How an armadillo is prepared for food by local Chinese was related to a "China Mail" reporter to-day.

label: text
text: The animal was on sale in Taipo last month and then brought down by train to Yaumati.

label: text
text: Preparation of an armadillo for a meal is somewhat similar to that for a hedgehog in Europe.

label: text
text: The body is wrapped up in clay and then roasted. When this "cooking" is over, the clay is knocked off and the scales of the armadillo come off at the same time without any trouble, leaving the meat. The heat is brought to an extent whereby the entrails shriveled up into a small ball which can be easily removed.

label: text
text: Believing the animal to have considerable dietary benefit, some Chinese pay high prices for this delicacy.
